text: I see a historical note suggesting Tuberculosis, but given your chief complaint of a scalp and forehead rash, that does not fit the typical clinical picture. To determine the actual cause, please describe the rash's appearance, whether it is itchy or painful, and if you have noticed any hair loss or recent sun exposure.

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the history of a red, scaly rash worsening in cold weather alongside a family history of psoriasis is very suggestive. To confirm if this is psoriasis or a related condition like seborrheic dermatitis, could you tell me if the rash involves your eyelids or if your baby has been scratching his head frequently? Also, have you noticed any scaling around the ears or eyebrows?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap). The combination of greasy yellow scales, erythematous patches on the scalp and forehead, and a family history of psoriasis in an infant is highly characteristic of this condition, which often mimics psoriasis.
